We got black precipitate with AgNO3. Black precipitate suggests Ag2S (silver sulfide) which is black, formed with sulfide (S2-). However sulfide is not in possible anions list? Actually S-2 is listed. So anion could be S2- (sulfide). But sample is inorganic salt, could be Na2S. That would give black Ag2S precipitate. Good.

But also could be AgI (yellow), AgBr (pale yellow), AgCl (white). Black is characteristic of Ag2S. So anion likely S2-.

We should confirm with other tests, e.g., add HCl to see H2S gas? Not needed. Could also add Ba(NO3)2 to see BaS? BaS is soluble, no precipitate. So not helpful.
